Hey, I'm a really small guy. I have to wear 14-16 in boys or XS in mens. However, XS is incredibly hard to find. Anyone else have this issue? Where are your guys' favourite places to shop, especially for formal wear, etc? I find that H&M XS fits me for casual clothes, and it's surprisingly hard to find nice formal stuff in children's sizes.
Adult men who don't fit into adult sizes: where do you shop?
Dillards or JC Pennys should have formalwear in those sizes.

I know your pain.... Most of the time, jeans and slacks come from the kids section at various places, t-shirts and polos, too. Sometimes I can find dress shirts in my size at Sears or Penney's in the menswear department...

Have you thought about buying made to measure?

PS: I'm 5'4", 114 lbs-ish.
I've thought about it. I probably will next time I have to go to a wedding, etc. because I'm tired of buying suits that are too big and getting them tailored.

I feel you. I am about average or slightly smaller than that (5'9" , 175) and I lift, so I'm heavy but not fat. I wear small and slim fit shirts. If I were any smaller, I don't know if I could find clothes at all. You can try lifting and eating more to fill out and then slim fit smalls will probably fit and look really good. Plus lifting when you are shorter means that you gain a lot really quickly.
I'm 5'2... 120. I don't think eating more and lifting weights is going to help much.
Yeah, but then how am I going to find wide and short?

You don't become that wide with lifting, it will just make it so that you fill out clothes where they need to be filled. There is a lifter at my gym that fills out smalls very well, and he is about 5'3" or so. What pants size are you measured for? usually you can find things down to 27x27 in men's, then for shirts you can tuck one end or all of it into the pants, and cuff the pants. Boom, now you look designer AF. For smaller guys, Express is the go-to. They have pretty alright stuff for cheap. The only reason I don't like their stuff on me is because it's for very very slim guys, and doesn't fit my style either. For people that lift, Polo Ralph Lauren is a good choice. They have various fits that are great, I usually go for the Slim or Custom (one wider) fits.

Going by BMI, amateur weightlifters usually fall around the "Overweight" BMI. I range from about 24.9-25.5 (Winter bulk). At that BMI, you would weigh 135, your waist and hips would be about the same, you would probably put a few inches around your chest and arms, and your legs would tighten up your pants a bit so you effectively gain an inch on the length.

The gains in your chest are going to be what make Small shirts fit better. There's no reason to get specifically wider shirts unless you are fat (NOT MUSCULAR).

Designer clothes would fit you. Do you not live close by a large shopping center? Express, Calvin Klein, Abercrombie and Fitch, shit like that. They would all have XS clothes.

Or you could lift weights for a couple years so you can wear mens small-medium and not look like you're wearing hammy-downs.

No Express near me although I like the Express that I find second hand. Abercrombie... I don't like. But I've had a lot of luck with H&M. My local mall is pretty small, but I should check the mall when I go to the big city.

Yea, designer clothes are your only hope. You may be able to score some XS designer shirts at a place like Marshalls, but their stock of clothes smaller than medium is very slim. I'm 5'7" and before I started weightlifting I would go to Marshalls and find a handful of shirts that weren't too big.
